memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses bowed to the ground at once and worshipped. 'Lord,' he said, 'if I have found favour in your eyes, then let the Lord go with us. Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our wickedness and our sin, and take us as your inheritance.'" - Exod 34:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses' first response to God's self-revelation is not a request. It is worship. He hits the ground.

That order matters. When we truly see who God is, asking comes second. Prayer that begins with adoration is prayer rightly ordered — which is why Jesus taught us to start with "hallowed be your name" before "give us today our daily bread" (Matt 6:9-11).

Then Moses asks, and notice how he does it. "Although this is a stiff-necked people" — he does not pretend. He does not tell God the people have improved. He agrees with God's assessment and asks for mercy anyway.

Notice also the pronoun shift: "forgive our wickedness and our sin." Moses does not stand above the people, pointing down. He includes himself. That is the mark of a shepherd rather than a critic.

Real intercession sounds like this. Honest about the sin, unashamed in asking for mercy, and standing alongside rather than above.

And Moses asks for something extraordinary: "take us as your inheritance." Not, give us an inheritance — make us Yours. In Christ, that is exactly what has happened. We are God's own possession, His treasured people (1 Pet 2:9; Titus 2:14).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your prayer begin with worship or with requests?
2. Are you honest with God about your own sin, or do you make excuses?
3. Do you pray for others as one standing above them or beside them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I bow before You first. I am no better than those I pray for — have mercy on us, and take us as Your own. Amen.
